claims.explanation: Levocetirizine selectively kills cancer cell lines that express the histamine H1 receptor (HRH1), because it antagonizes HRH1-mediated survival/proliferation signals; the virtual cell's similarity to chlorphenamine supports this on-target mechanism. Additional weaker features may include sensitizing ATM mutations and protective NF1/PTEN mutations, which respectively impair DNA damage response or activate RAS/PI3K survival pathways.

features.basis: Drug target; H1 antagonist blocks histamine-driven proliferation
Damaging mutation in 3 sensitive lines (SNUC5, 786O, SNU685) and 0 resistant; ATM loss impairs DNA damage response
Damaging mutation in 4 resistant lines (FTC133, S117, KALS1, LOXIMVI) vs 1 sensitive; NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK survival
Damaging mutation in 4 resistant lines (FTC133, ZR751, KALS1, HEC265) vs 2 sensitive; PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT survival
Damaging mutation in 4 sensitive lines (SNUC5, BICR6, KU1919, KYSE270) vs 2 resistant; KMT2D loss may alter chromatin and increase HRH1 dependence
Damaging mutation in 3 sensitive lines (MHHES1, IPC298, SNU1214) vs 1 resistant; cell cycle deregulation may sensitize to antiproliferative effect
Damaging mutation in 3 sensitive lines (SNUC5, MKN1, CL11) vs 1 resistant; FBXW7 loss may cause genomic instability
Damaging mutation in 3 resistant lines (T3M4, FTC133, OV7) vs 1 sensitive; KMT2C loss may promote survival
